findings.title: Access-token matcher does not validate the expected grant
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies indices 4 through 5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5). It also returns false when the substring equals the expected grant, rather than when it differs. Consequently, the authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA event assertions accept tokens with incorrect or unknown grants, hiding failures to propagate the grant context. Validate the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

findings.title: Document the required two-character grant shortcut
findings.body: The new SPI documentation recommends a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an encoded context of exactly six characters and reserves exactly two characters for the grant. A custom grant following this documented contract will issue token IDs that the default decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Document the exact two-character requirement and validate it when registering grant factories so incompatible shortcuts cannot silently produce undecodable tokens.

findings.title: Unknown-grant test passes on an unrelated NullPointerException
findings.body: The test factory is initialized manually without postInit(), leaving its sessionFactory null. Decoding the unregistered 'ac' shortcut therefore throws NullPointerException in getGrantTypeByShortcut() while attempting to refresh the mapping, before the decoder can throw its intended IllegalArgumentException. Catching any RuntimeException makes this test pass without exercising unknown-grant validation. Provide a mocked session factory with no matching grant and assert the specific IllegalArgumentException.
